facts.statement: Dakotadon is a genus of iguanodont dinosaur known for its distinctive teeth.
facts.quote: Dakotadon (meaning "Dakota tooth") is a genus of iguanodont dinosaur

facts.statement: The genus is known from a partial skull fossil.
Dakotadon was first described in 1989 as the species Iguanodon lakotaensis by paleontologists David B. Weishampel and Philip R. Bjork.
facts.quote: It was first described in 1989 as Iguanodon lakotaensis, by David B. Weishampel and Philip R. Bjork

facts.statement: A partial skull and associated skeleton were brought to the attention of John Willard in November 1985.
facts.quote: In November 1985, a partial skull and associated skeleton was brought to the attention of South Dakota School of Mines and Technology professor emeritus John Willard

facts.statement: The fossil material was originally found by Louis Rossow in outcrops near Whitewood, South Dakota.
facts.quote: The material had been found earlier by Louis Rossow, who collected geological specimens from outcrops on homesteads in Whitewood, South Dakota

facts.statement: The specimen was donated to the South Dakota School of Mines and Technology Museum and accessioned as SDSM 8656.
facts.quote: The specimen was donated to the museum, being accessioned as SDSM 8656

facts.statement: Dakotadon lived during the Early Cretaceous (Valanginian to Barremian) in the Lakota Formation of South Dakota, USA.
facts.quote: from the Early Cretaceous (Valanginian to Barremian) Lakota Formation of South Dakota, USA

facts.statement: Revised stratigraphic analysis dates Dakotadon to the late Valanginian to early Barremian, an older age than previously thought.
facts.quote: This gives Dakotadon a late Valanginian to early Barremian age, older than most previous assessments

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated Dakotadon to be 6 meters long and have a body mass of 1 metric ton.
facts.quote: He measured its length at 6 m and body mass at 1 MT

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul established the genus Dakotadon for I. lakotaensis in 2008.
facts.quote: Gregory S. Paul, working on a revision of iguanodont species, gave "I." lakotaensis its own genus, Dakotadon, in 2008

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul classified Dakotadon as a basal iguanodont that falls outside the families Iguanodontidae and Iguanodontoidea.
facts.quote: who also found it was a more basal iguanodont outside Iguanodontidae and Iguanodontoidea

facts.statement: Dakotadon belongs to the infraorder Ornithopoda.
Dakotadon is classified within the unranked family Iguanodontia.

The classification of Dakotadon is controversial; while some researchers view it as a distinct basal iguanodont related to Theiophytalia, David Norman has argued it is a synonym of Iguanodon bernissartensis.
facts.quote: Its assignment has been controversial. Some researchers suggested that "I." lakotaensis was more basal than I. bernissartensis, and related to Theiophytalia, but David Norman has suggested that it was a synonym of I. bernissartensis

facts.statement: Weishampel and Bjork noted that despite sharing unique features with European Iguanodon species, Dakotadon had fewer teeth and other traits suggesting it was more distantly related.
facts.quote: Weishampel and Bjork considered I. lakotaensis to share features unique to the other established Iguanodon species, I. atherfieldensis and I. bernissartensis, which are both from the Barremian of Europe. However, despite its slightly larger size than I. atherfieldensis, I. lakotaensis had fewer teeth and some other features to suggest than it was more distantly related than the two European species

facts.statement: In spring 2014, researchers returned to the original fossil site east of Whitewood, guided by the grandchildren of the original discoverer Louis Rossow.
facts.quote: In spring 2014, they returned to the site, east of Whitewood, being guided by the grandchildren of Louis Rossow

facts.statement: The time range for Dakotadon is estimated to be between 137.05 and 132.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Valanginian to Valanginian (137.05 to 132.6 million years ago)

facts.statement: Dakotadon is notable for being the most complete Early Cretaceous dinosaur known from the Black Hills region.
facts.quote: The importance of Dakotadon as the most complete Early Cretaceous dinosaur from the Black Hills region

rejected.statement: After re-preparation, the complete holotype of Dakotadon included a partial skull, lower jaws, and dorsal and caudal vertebrae.
rejected.quote: The complete holotype of Dakotadon after repreparation included a partial skull, lower jaws, and dorsal and caudal vertebrae
